```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2movies)
```

For my final project, I plan to compare the popularity and sales of two movie genres in the United States: action and comedy. I want to understand which genre audiences choose more often, and whether that has changed over time.

To start, I am using the IMDb movie data in the ggplot2movies package. The most interesting variables for my project are the release year, the genre, the average IMDb rating, the number of votes a movie received (a good measure of popularity), and the budget. Later, I plan to add box office sales from a source like The Numbers so I can compare how much money each genre earns in the United States, not just how many people rate it.

```{r}
genre_movies <- movies |>
  filter(year >= 1950, year <= 2004) |>
  mutate(genre = case_when(
    Action == 1 & Comedy == 0 ~ "Action",
    Comedy == 1 & Action == 0 ~ "Comedy"
  )) |>
  filter(!is.na(genre))

genre_movies |>
  summarize(count = n(), .by = c(year, genre)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = count, color = genre)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 1.5) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Action = "#d1495b", Comedy = "#7b2cbf")) +
  labs(
    title = "Comedies Far Outnumber Action Movies",
    subtitle = "Number of movies released each year, 1950 to 2004",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Number of movies",
    color = "Genre",
    caption = "Source: IMDb data from the ggplot2movies package"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        legend.position = "top")
```
